sources.entry: llvm-objdump - Reads the binary that shipped, with source lines and symbolised branch targets, rather than a recompiled snippet.

summary.title: llvm-objdump - LLVM's object file dumper
summary.one_liner: llvm-objdump is LLVM's command-line tool for dumping object files and linked binaries, including disassembly with source lines, symbolized branch targets, headers, relocations and symbol tables.
takeaways: Use -d to disassemble executable sections, -D to disassemble all sections, or --disassemble=<symbol> for one symbol.
Add -S or -l to interleave source lines with the disassembly.
--symbolize-operands replaces raw branch addresses with labels; bb-address-map data is used when present.
Options like -t (symbols), -r (relocations), -h (section headers) and -x (all headers) dump other file metadata.
Architecture-specific behaviour (--mcpu, --mattr, --disassembler-options such as att/intel on x86) is controlled by flags.
summary.summary: This is the official LLVM command guide reference page for llvm-objdump. It lists the synopsis, commands (such as -d, -D, -h, -r, -t, -x), and a long set of options covering disassembly control, source interleaving, symbolization, disassembler colour and syntax, and Mach-O, XCOFF-only flags. The page is a reference rather than a tutorial, so it is best used to look up specific flags.
